recipe.title: Chard, smoked haddock and new potato frittata
recipe.intro: Chard is coming thick and fast in early June, and its tender leaves and crunchy stalks bulk out a frittata beautifully alongside the first new potatoes.
steps: Boil the new potatoes in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes until tender. Drain, leave to cool a little, then slice thickly.

Meanwhile, put the haddock in a small frying pan, cover with the milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes until it flakes easily. Lift out, flake into large pieces and discard the skin. Keep 3 tbsp of the milk.

Thinly slice the chard stalks and shred the leaves. Heat the oil in the ovenproof pan and cook the stalks and spring onions for 5 minutes until soft. Add the leaves and stir for 2 minutes until wilted.
Heat the grill to high. Whisk the eggs with the saved milk, the chives, half the cheese, plenty of pepper and a small pinch of salt, as the haddock is already salty.
Spread the potatoes and haddock over the chard, pour in the eggs and cook on a low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until the edges are set but the middle still wobbles.
Scatter over the rest of the cheese and grill for 3 to 5 minutes until puffed, golden and just set in the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into wedges and serve warm with the salad leaves.
recipe.tip: Leftover wedges keep in the fridge for 2 days and are lovely cold in a lunchbox. Fresh cod works too, just add a little more salt.
